name: Peshtigo River
gnis_history: An Indian word meaning "wild goose river."

name: Llano River
gnis_history: A Spanish phrase meaning "river of the plain."

name: Neosho River
gnis_history: An Indian word meaning "clear cold water."

name: Minnesota River
gnis_history: The name Minnesota was originally given to the river by the Dakota Indians and was recorded as "Waddapawmenesotor" by Carver in 1767. In Santee dialect "watpa" means river and "mi'-ni-so-ta" means "whitish water." The name was given to the river for its cloudy appearance from the silt it carried. Romantics misconstrued this name and incorrectly rendered it as "sky blue water" and "sky tinted water." (KS-T33/p199)

name: Wabash River
gnis_history: The name is derived from the Miami name. The Indian translation suggests that it was named for being white, bright, inanimate, or natural. Speculation is that this refers to a limestone bed in the upper part of the stream. (IN-T101/p336)

name: Susan River
gnis_history: Susan River was named for Susan Roop, daughter of Issac Roop, an early settler.

name: Merrimack River
gnis_history: "Merrimack " is an Indian word meaning "sound of the falls," (MGB 1932) Sturgeon, or swift water (Steel) (Douglas-Lithgow 1909).

name: Middle Fork North Fork Klaskanine River
Thomas Creek
gnis_history: Thomas Creek was named for Frederick Thomas, who obtained a donation land claim on the banks of the stream in 1846.

name: Black Warrior River
gnis_history: A translation of the Choctaw Indian word tuscaloosa.

name: Roanoke River
gnis_history: First named Hocomawananch by the Indian population; name Rorenock was applied by European settlers in 1670. Col. Cadwallader Jones labeled it the Occaneechi River on his 1693 map; labeled Staunton River on 1727 survey of Virginia-North Carolina boundary. An Indian word designating a kind of shell used for money.

name: Missouri River
gnis_history: The popular but erroneous conception that the name means "muddy water" arose from the fact that Marquette gave it the indigenous name "Pekitanoui" meaning "muddy".  Early white explorers first called the stream "Missouri" after a tribe of Indians who lived on its banks and whose name meant "people with wooden canoes." (Robert Ramsay placename file).  The variant name "Emasulia Sipiwi" means "river of boatmen" in the Peoria language.

name: Scioto River
gnis_history: Coordinates verified.

name: Allegheny River
gnis_history: Delaware Indian name meaning 'fine river' or 'beautiful river'.

name: Yellow Water Creek
gnis_history: Name in use since 1880's

name: Ohio River
gnis_history: An Iroquois Indian word meaning "beautiful river."

name: Pemigewasset River
gnis_history: The word is of Indian derivation, said to mean "crooked place of pines."

name: Little East Fork Ohio Brush Creek
Potomac River
gnis_history: Heads at the junction of North Branch Potomac River and South Branch Potomac River on the Maryland-West Virginia boundary 2.4 km (1.5 mi) SE of Oldtown, Maryland, flows southeasterly into the Chesapeake Bay south of Point Lookout. Lowest elevation in DC at 1 foot. Lowest elevation in WV at 240 feet.

name: Escambia River
gnis_history: Although the name may be derived from the Spanish word 'cambiar,' meaning to exchange or barter, it more likely is from an Indian word of unknown meaning.

name: Sacramento River
gnis_history: Named by the Spaniards, the word meaning "sacrament."

name: Monocacy River
gnis_history: An Indian word meaning "stream containing many large bends."

name: Ochlockonee River
gnis_history: A Creek Indian word meaning "yellow water."

name: Platte River
gnis_history: "The name 'Platte' is French for flat & was given by Canadian hunters because the stream for much of its length is broad, shallow, and flat but still below the wide level valley.  It is pre-eminently the flat river" (US-T121).

name: Pascagoula River
gnis_history: The lower eight miles of the Pascagoula River are known locally as the Singing River.

name: Chattahoochee River
gnis_history: Name is reportedly Muskogean (Creek), meaning 'rocks-marked', from _chato_ 'rock' plus _huchi_ 'marked'. ("Place Names of Alabama", Virginia Foscue, 1989)

name: Snake River
gnis_history: Name possibly derived from an S-shaped (snake) sign which the Shoshone Indians made with their hands to mimic swimming salmon.

name: Tchefuncte River
gnis_history: Indian name.

name: Jacks Creek
gnis_history: Named for John (Jack) Turner, rancher, who arrived in Little Valley in 1869.

name: Skunk River
gnis_history: A translation of the Indian name Checauqua.

name: Ocmulgee River
gnis_history: A Creek Indian word meaning "boiling water."
